title: S$15 hi! 30-Day Tourist eSIM 500GB (SG, MY, ID, TH, HK​) + 18GB (APAC, China, S. Korea, Japan​) + 8GB (60+ Countries) @ Singtel
body:
Deal: S$15 hi! 30-Day Tourist eSIM 500GB (SG, MY, ID, TH, HK​) + 18GB (APAC, China, S. Korea, Japan​) + 8GB (60+ Countries) @ Singtel

[nguyentran] For Vietnam, buy a local sim card or buy @ klook is cheaper
[dasher86] Klook is crap these days for Vietnam.
Trip.com is better.
[caustic birch] Worth changing the currency on klook. I paid 25 HKD (5 AUD) for a Europe esim listed as 20 AUD
[Duoka] Both are included in APAC roaming $15 and $30 plans
[Deal Hunting] Does the data in this eSim still work without activating in Singapore? If not then it's a bit niche
[Duoka] According to their chatbot, Yes, you can register and activate your hi! Tourist eSIM bought from the Singtel website outside Singapore, as long as your phone supports eSIM and is connected to the Internet. Do note: if you registered using a passport, you will have data-only service until you complete in-person verification at a Singtel Shop/authorised hi! retailer in Singapore to enable calls and SMS.
[Deal Hunting] Can someone test this out? I wonder if this deal is long term? The price is unbeatable if so
[nathanos] I can confirm this works well. Both my mate and I bought the S$15 eSIM a couple months back when we went to Malaysia and Singapore. We activated it before we left Australia. We flew straight to Malaysia and it was working perfectly without connecting to Singtel in Singapore first.
The service was decent in Malaysia and very good in Singapore (as would be expected).
We didn't bother trying to enable the calls/SMS as WhatsApp/Signal were all we needed. If you wanted to use this long term, I'm pretty sure you'd need to buy a new service every month which would mean physically presenting yourself and passport at a Singtel store each month to enable calls/SMS.
My mate bought a TuneTalk eSIM in Malaysia for RM35 and it was better quality than the Singtel roaming eSIM, but the Singtel one was more than usable for the price/convenience of not needing multiple eSIMs (and I personally used it the entire week I was in Malaysia with no issues).
[Rewards Granted] Is it safe to assume that all esims can bypass China’s firewall?
[SetTheFaqUp] Yes even ones from Hong Kong (which is also part of the PRC).
[HyperZ] As long as it routes traffic outside of China (check APN)… speeds vary with eSIMs from budget carriers like Billionconnect/Redteago sometimes worth paying slightly more
[nathanos] "APAC roaming" with the 20 destinations includes Australia + New Zealand

[gviddy] $30 for 700GB and 80GB roaming. Wow! Thanks for nothing Australian mobile providers!
[Russ] Approximately 3 million square kilometres of Australia (Telstra figures) has mobile coverage. The entirety of Singapore is 744 square kilometres, so about 4000 times smaller.
There's a reason why it's cheaper in Singapore, the mobile network cost way less to build. And Singtel is government owned, so they don't have to make a profit and pay dividends.
[FujinShu] But then again, Singtel also owns Optus, so if anything, you could say that Optus is subsidising Singtel.
[ozrekeno] I own Singtel shares and they do pay dividends.
[Russ] I stand corrected.
I've checked, and the Singapore government owns 49.8% of the shares in Singtel. So for the rest of the shareholders to get control, more than 99.5% of them would have to vote against the government.
So I should have said effectively government owned, and I was wrong about the dividends.

[Russ] According to this webpage , "In the secure/transit area and the arrivals hall, many kiosks and businesses at Singapore Changi Airport offer Singtel, StarHub, and M1 Singapore tourist SIM cards."
So if you're transiting through Changi on your way to somewhere else, you may be able to purchase and activate the eSIM at the airport, and get the full features.
[illumination] If you do that, you could probably find a similar product for a bit cheaper on a different telco, and possibly on a physical SIM instead if you prefer that

I wish if they had a 90 days package.

[HyperZ] Can confirm this works well in Hong Kong, mainland China (Shenzhen), Taiwan (Taipei), Japan (Tokyo) and the Philippines.
I also had a StarHub eSIM active at the same time. The only place where StarHub provided noticeably better speeds and stability was the Philippines, particularly around Manila and Alabang.
I purchased and activated the Singtel eSIM before leaving Australia and confirmed that roaming data was working. Data usage also tracked correctly in the Singtel app. I bought it directly from Singtel before they started redirecting customers to Pelago.
The StarHub eSIM was purchased through Pelago at around the same time, but I could never get it to link properly with the StarHub app, so I wasn’t able to track usage.
In Hong Kong, my 3HK DIY local eSIM with 365-day validity and the Greater Bay Area roaming pack was faster than both Singtel and StarHub. This was the case both within Hong Kong and when crossing the border into Shenzhen. It uses a local IP in Hong Kong, although ChatGPT was unavailable. I keep this 3HK with the global roaming pack for HK268 per year, together with the roamless global eSIM for emergencies.
In mainland China, my local China Mobile 5G SIM was the fastest option for local services such as WeChat. However, Google, Facebook, Meta services and ChatGPT were blocked unless I connected through NordVPN or TorGuard. Singtel and StarHub worked without any issues, including access to those services.
In the Philippines, both Globe and Smart were patchy, as coverage varied considerably across Manila. Overall, I found StarHub better than Singtel for both speed and stability.
In Tokyo, the best speeds and stability came from an AU/KDDI prepaid SIM with a local IP. That said, both Singtel and StarHub still worked fine.
One useful tip for anyone getting the Singtel eSIM: speeds appear to be capped at around 10 Mbps down and 10 Mbps up when using the default hicard APN. Changing the APN to e-ideas removed the cap for me and allowed access to the full available network speed.
For reference the eSIMs above is used on either the iPhone 15 Pro Max or Samsung Fold 7 with 9eSIM.
[Solario31] Bugger flying to japan and china in october, wish it had a longer validity.
[illumination] You could just buy it shortly before your trip. This isn't a limited time offer, and going by the state of the Singapore telco market over the last year, the inclusions are likely to get less generous (if anything, it could get more generous)
